standard_prerequisites.name: Every coherent sheaf is the pushforward of a coherent sheaf on the closed subscheme given by its support
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology of Schemes, labels coherent-lemma-coherent-support-closed (proof line 2018) and coherent-proposition-proper-pushforward-coherent (used in the statement at proof lines 2008-2011)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the closed immersion i : Z -> X and the coherent O_Z-module G with i_* G isomorphic to F, which is the first reduction of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of the generic fibre and the pushdown formula for a finite ring map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, labels morphisms-lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image (proof line 2042) and morphisms-lemma-generically-finite (proof line 2069); same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-multiplicity-finite (proof line 2066); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-pushdown-module (proof line 2094)
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes f|_Z dominant and, after shrinking to an open neighbourhood of the generic point, finite and affine, and finally converts the coefficient of Z in f_*[F]_k into the sum over the primes of A over p via the pushdown formula.

core_obligations: Reduce part (1) to part (2) via the identification of the cycle class of a closed subscheme with that of its structure sheaf, and reduce part (2) in general to the case of a dominant proper morphism with dim_delta(X) at most k by factoring F through its support: write F = i_* G, let Z' be the scheme theoretic image of f|_Z so that f_* F = i'_* (f|_Z)_* G, and chase the cycle classes around the square (proof lines 2014-2044).

In the reduced situation show that any integral Z occurring with nonzero coefficient in either f_*[F]_k or [f_*F]_k is an irreducible component of Y of delta-dimension exactly k, that f^{-1}(eta) is finite because only finitely many generic points of components of X of dimension k lie over the generic point eta, and hence, after shrinking Y, that f is finite and affine (proof lines 2046-2072).

Finish in the affine finite case: write Y = Spec(R), X = Spec(A) with A finite over R and F the sheaf associated with a finite A-module M; the coefficient of Z in [f_*F]_k is length_{R_p}(M_p) while the coefficient in f_*[F]_k is the sum over the primes q_i of A over p of the residue degree times length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}), and these agree by the pushdown formula for finite ring maps (proof lines 2074-2094).
proof_roadmap: Reduce both parts to the case of a dominant proper f with dim_delta(X) at most k, using the support decomposition of F (proof lines 2014-2044).
Shrink to a neighbourhood of the generic point where f becomes finite and affine (proof lines 2046-2072).
Compare the multiplicities in the affine finite case and invoke the pushdown formula (proof lines 2074-2094).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a proper f : X -> Y and a coherent F whose support has delta-dimension at most k, the cycle class of the pushforward equals the pushforward of the cycle class, in the form f_*[F]_k = [f_*F]_k, with the corresponding statement for a closed subscheme (statement lines 1991-2012, tag 02R6). The proof is a real reduction rather than a citation: it factors F through its support, reduces to a dominant proper morphism, shows that the generic fibre over any relevant component of Y is finite and shrinks to make f finite and affine, and then compares the multiplicities through the pushdown formula for a finite ring map. The reduction and the multiplicity comparison are both carried out in the span, so the claim is H2.
